notes:
Things to check:
1. Rows for lights not yet lit: Bull Point (p37r15, 'to be completed summer 1879') and Langness (p42r2, 'Light proposed'). Neither row gives a position or a working character. Decide whether these count as matches or should be null.
2. Tees No. 5 Buoy (p45r4): the row's name is blank in the transcription. Check the scan to confirm what heads it.
3. Casquets, Hanois and Heligoland aren't in this table. Casquets and Hanois should be in Findlay's Channel Islands section; Heligoland would be under another country. I've returned null for all three, but they probably have entries elsewhere.
4. Stations returned null as not yet built or placed: South Gare, Selker LV, Dee LV, Anvil Point. Dee LV is the least certain; make sure it isn't the Liverpool N.W. Lightship (p40r9).
5. Stations that aren't lights (null): Great Cotes, Northrepps, the second 1880 Teesmouth entry, North Stack fog station, Lundy fog gun station, and Allonby (printed 'L.H.', but Findlay has no light there).
6. Shared rows: one row covers each pair. St Ann's Head (p39r2) goes to all three St Ann's ids and Nash Point (p38r10) to both Nash ids.
7. No station needed extra_rows: every high/low pair in this table is printed in a single row.
8. Rows with no position of their own: Landguard Point (p43r2), Great Castle Head (p39r3), Falmouth/St Anthony (p36r17), Shambles (p36r7), Bull Sand LV (p44r13), Tees 5 buoy (p45r4). Positions for these will have to come from somewhere else.
9. Tongue LV (p33r11): Findlay says the vessel was sunk in July 1877, so the 1879 description may not fit the vessel the keepers reported from.
